cells.location: Bantra
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Mahālingēśvara temple in the village.
cells.remarks: In characters of about the 8th century A.D. Refers to the rule of a Katamba (Kadamba) king. Seems to register an agreement regarding the enjoyment of some lands, made by the king and his chief, Rācamalla-Dugārāja of Vilāṭṭali-yarasu and Narasingan-Dugārāja and some Perggades. States that a golden pinnacle was set up over the temple of Pañcahaligēśvara at Iṣṭakāpura by Muṇḍi-Seṭṭi of Pañcahaligēśvara, and that a certain Dēvappa-Dēva of Domba-Vergado having been cured of disease, on a stone monument here is a modern Malayalam inscription of Narasiṁharāja of Viṭṭhala. States that Kumhicēvarasa alias Doriba-Hogade of Viṭṭhala set up this (water-trough) for cows, to secure merit.
